answer: Harbor delivery commitment bars mass forgery. A newcomer docks at the harbor, stakes a pearl bond of 70 credits, and pledges one genuine task by next tide. The kernel audits deliveries against the public log; a copied or missed one burns the bond. Forging a thousand identities costs 45 first, then 6 more each: 3,042,000 plus 70,000 locked, while the pool holds only 40,000. A truthful agent pays 45 once and keeps its full portion.
